segments.text: And for such a yogi di-vashāth sattu-siddhi, by conducting his reality of intellect,
supreme intellect, de means here supreme intellect.
It is not ordinary intellect.
By that intellect, sattu-siddhi, sāthik abhenea, sāthik abhenea is achieved by yogi.
Yogis feel that he is actually acting.
There are some yogis who are acting in Rajas abhenea.
They feel on sidelines that they are acting in this universal drama.
There are some tamas possessing tamas abhenea of this drama and they feel
that they are only feeling that they are playing in this drama is only through imagination,
not actual.
But for those who possess sattik abhenea, they feel actually that they are playing.
There is no doubt about it for them.
So that sattik abhenea takes place only when there is that supreme intellect filled with awareness,
filled with the awareness of self.
That is the explanation of de-vashāth sattu-siddhi.
Sattu means sattik abhenea.
Real, it is not only copy, copying, it is not only imitation, it is reality.
He feels that he is really acting.
He is really acting as Radhakarīn.
He is really acting as John and everything.
So intellect de-tātek sarūpu-ymarsana-vishāradha.
That intellect which is skillful in perceiving the real nature.
Vishāradha means skillful.
That which is skillful in perceiving the real nature.
That intellect is held here.
And it is vishadādisana.
And this intellect is absolutely pure.
Vishadā means pure.
Tādvashāth satta-suprata-atmanā-sukshmāsya antar pārspandāsya-siddhi-rādivakti-rbavati.
By that, by conducting that kind of intellect,
that kind of supreme pure intellect,
that reality of self takes place in internal way.
In drama also, in outward drama also, nāteja-sāyatik abhenea-siddhi-rbuddhi-kāvśala-thevar labhete.
There is sāyatik abhenea.
Sāyatik abhenea is only achieved by maintaining,
by possessing the reality of intellect,
real way of intellect.
And this acting is the imitation of condition.
And this acting is forefold.
Angik acting, vajik, ahari and sāyatik.
Angik means conveyed by bodily actions.
His bodily actions, bodily actions of hero must be adopted in such a way
that you will feel this is the body of Rama.
This is not the body of that actor.
You must feel, every spectator must feel that this is the body of Rama, actual Rama.
So, they must get thrilled by perceiving that.
This is bodily actions.
This is called angik abhenea.
Second is vajik, conveyed by words.
You must feel, the spectators must feel that these words are uttered by Rama himself, not actor.
This is the way Sāyatik abhenea is held by heroes,
not by ordinary players.
Ahari is third way of abhenea.
It is conveyed by dress and ornaments.
These dress and ornaments must be held in such a way by spectators that these ornaments are really possessed by Rama, not by actor.
These are his.
Spectators must feel that and this is called sāyatik abhenea.
Third is ahariya, by internal feeling.
That is smiling, weeping etc.
That is ahariya.
For instance, if he is sad, he will make all spectators sad.
If he is acting in sāyatik abhenea in the way of sāyatik abhenea, he will make you all sad.
Or if he is weeping, he will also weep with him.
You will actually feel that he is really in misery, in sadness.
And you will become also sad.
This is the way Sāyatik abhenea is conducted by players in Rama.
